title: Share one import skeleton between two importers

task.text: Refactor to a **template method**: one abstract class owns the fixed sequence, and each importer supplies only what differs. `run(List<String>)`, `saved()` and `log()` must behave exactly as they do now, including logging `close` when a row fails.

items: Move the skeleton (open, skip blank lines, parse, filter minors, store, report, close) into one abstract superclass of both importers.
Its `run(List<String>)` is `final`. The steps subclasses fill in are not `public`.
`CsvImporter` and `PipeImporter` keep their no-argument constructors and contain only format knowledge: how to split a row, and that pipe files ignore `#` lines.

checks.title: A bad row still logs close
Both importers extend one abstract class
The abstract steps are not public

hints.text: Compare the two classes line by line. The order of the steps is identical; only splitting a row and the comment rule differ. The sequence is what should be written once.
Create an abstract class holding `saved`, `log` and a `final run`. Add an abstract `parse(String)` step and a hook `ignore(String)` with a default. Both importers extend it.
The skeleton calls the steps, and the subclass fills them:

lines: protected boolean ignore(String line) { return false; }
